title: Jobs and contributions
teach: An occupation is a job. A contribution is what that work provides for society. Name the job, describe what the person does, and connect the work to what others need.

teachingSections.title: Jobs and contributions
teachingSections.where: Read the assigned OER PDF, pages 15, 16, 17.
teach: An occupation is a job. A contribution is what that work provides for society. Name the job, describe what the person does, and connect the work to what others need.
Scribes read, wrote and kept records, including taxes, court cases and a census, which is a population count. Artisans made goods such as pottery, furniture and jewelry.

Farmers grew food and useful crops and raised animals. Food surplus means extra food beyond what is needed. A surplus helped some people specialize in other jobs. People depended on one another’s work.

For three specific contributions, name different useful tasks. Scribes could keep tax records, count soldiers and record a census. Artisans could make pottery, furniture and jewelry. Farmers could grow food, grow useful crops such as flax and raise animals.

Connect each task to a result. A tax record helps officials track what was collected; a census records the population; food and useful crops support people in other occupations. Three different words for one task are not three different contributions.

example.prompt: A scribe records how much wheat people pay in taxes. How does this work help the government?
example.thinking: The task is record keeping, not growing wheat. The record tells officials what has been collected.
example.answer: A scribe’s tax record helps officials track grain collected. For three distinct contributions, a scribe could also record the army’s size and a census of the population.
example.why: This connects the worker’s action to a useful result.

teachingSections.tryPrompt: Which worker makes pottery as a skilled craft?
teachingSections.tryAnswer: An artisan. Artisans used specialized skills to make goods such as pottery.

connections.prompt: How did extra food help people specialize in other jobs?
options: Some people could learn a craft while farmers supplied food.
Extra food meant all farming work could stop permanently.
A census automatically taught each person a new craft.
connections.rationale: Some people could learn a craft while farmers supplied food. Connect a job with what it provides, then identify the government offices that use those services.

connections.prompt: A grower supplies food and a potter supplies storage jars. Which connection fits?
options: Different occupations provide goods each can use.
The two occupations perform exactly the same task.
Each person can meet every need without other workers.
connections.rationale: Different occupations provide goods each can use. A grocer needs food from growers, and growers need goods and services. Modern workers do not have the same social classes as ancient Egyptians.
